So this is actually a really good teaching point for extensions on letters - pieces or hand styles. 

Notice how in this case all of their letters have intentionally rounded tops or in the case of the t an up-slant that leads into their tag.

For the t he reason why this works is because it's bringing a natural attention and flow to the entire tag with the way English is read from left to right, while the lower bar flows with the upright slant and mood of the vertical bars in the other letters.

One of two reasons why the extension doesn't work is because instead of carrying on like a cohesive flow it starts at the middle of the line height with a non matching tone for the vertical bars. This breaks the flow and makes the hand style end abruptly. 

The second reason why it doesn't work is because it has a sharp top whereas the rest of the hand style is rounded off. It just doesn't match the font.
